newsitem.title: GERMANY: Santer says sticks to strict reading of Maastricht.
newsitem.headline: Santer says sticks to strict reading of Maastricht.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Tuesday that he was sticking to the view that the Maastricht Treaty for economic and monetary union (EMU) should be strictly adhered to.

Asked whether a budget deficit of more than 3.0 percent of Gross Domestic Product would be acceptable for entry to EMU Santer said: "We are always sticking to a restrictive interpretation of the criteria."
Santer was speaking to reporters on the fringes of the Global 24 conference on monetary union.
He also said he was confident EMU would start on time in January 1999 and that it would be a stable currency.
"I think there are real reasons that EMU would come on time... and it would be a stable and strong currency," he said.
